post.description: Research keyword data (search volume, difficulty, CPC, related ideas) for 1-5 seed keywords in one call — one research run per seed. Returns `results`, one entry per seed with `ok` — a single bad seed won't fail the batch. CHARGES CREDITS ON THE PAID DATA PROVIDER: per seed, ~30-100 credits each dep

projectId.description: Required. The MisarSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

locationCode.description: DataForSEO location code. Omit it to use the project's default market, which falls back to 2840 (United States) for a project that has not set one. See dataforseo.com/help-center/locations. Some countries (e.g. Iceland, 2352) are served from Google Ads data: keyword volume/CPC/trends work, but keyword difficulty, search intent, and domain analytics are unavailable.

languageCode.description: Language code (e.g. 'en', 'es', 'fr'). Omit it to use the project's default market language, which falls back to 'en'.

seeds.description: 1-5 seed keywords. Each seed is researched independently and returns related keywords with volume/difficulty/CPC. Bulk-friendly — prefer this over multiple single-seed calls.

resultLimit.description: Cap on the data provider's own rows per seed. Defaults to 150. It is NOT a cap on `rowCount`: free Google Suggest ideas are appended after the cap is applied, so a seed can legitimately report more rows than this number.

includeClickstreamData.description: Refine search volumes with clickstream data, which disaggregates Google Ads' grouped close-variant volumes (plurals/misspellings). On the paid DataForSEO provider this DOUBLES the credit cost of each seed. Default false (standard Google-Ads-derived volumes). Ignored — no cost, no effect — for countries served from Google Ads data, and on the free data provider, whose autocomplete + Keyword Planner sources have no clickstream refinement at all.

post.description: Query the connected Search Console property's Search Analytics: clicks, impressions, CTR, and average position by query/page/country/device/date. First-party data — use it for what already ranks, near-ranking queries, and pages with real demand. ctr is a 0-1 fraction; position is a 1-based average;

projectId.description: Required. The MisarSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

dimensions.description: Group rows by these dimensions. Default ['query']. Use ['page'] for top pages, ['query','page'] to map queries to pages / spot cannibalization, ['date'] for a time series.

dateRange.description: Convenience window (default last_28_days). End is set ~3 days back for GSC data lag. Ignored if startDate+endDate are given. Max lookback is 16 months.

startDate.description: Explicit start (YYYY-MM-DD, Pacific Time). Use with endDate.

endDate.description: Explicit end (YYYY-MM-DD, Pacific Time). Use with startDate.

filters.description: AND-combined filters. To get the queries for one page: [{dimension:'page',operator:'equals',expression:'https://example.com/post'}] with dimensions ['query'].

rowLimit.description: Rows per call (default 1000, max 1000). GSC sorts by clicks desc and can't filter by position — filter 'striking distance' positions client-side, and paginate with startRow when hasMore is true.

post.description: Finds the queries where the project's connected Search Console property competes with itself: two or more of its own pages drawing impressions for the same query, splitting that query's clicks, click signals and ranking history across URLs. Read-only and FREE (no credits) — Search Console is first-p

projectId.description: Required. The MisarSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

window.description: Analysis window (default last_28_days). Capped at three months on purpose — Search Console's longer ranges are NOT offered, because over a long window 'two pages received impressions' also describes a page migration, and calling that cannibalisation sends someone to consolidate pages that are already consolidated. The window end is backed off ~3 days for Search Console's data lag.

sort.description: Finding order (default impressions). 'impressions' = most affected search demand first. 'position_spread' = smallest gap between the competing pages' average positions first, i.e. the pages Google rated most interchangeable. Both order by one measured quantity; there is deliberately no composite severity score.
